previous_reply_acts.text: (your request) Yes. codex-17 is taking over the seat: I've written it a handoff and belled it (`invoke-…b504795c`). Its first step is to read the handoff, check the chart and the five open jobs, and send you a short status confirming it holds the seat. previous_reply_acts.author: claude-4
previous_reply_acts.text:
(what the handoff contains) It's in `/tmp/pyreg/overnight/HANDOFF-codex-17.md` and covers:
- the goal, the branch and file locations, and how to run tests and probes
- your standing rules (emulate Lean, 3-file jobs, tests that fail at the base, byte checks, Zai first)
- how I review: run the test at the base, plant a bug, check the Lean citations, with recent examples of the problems caught
- the five open jobs with their ids and what to do when each finishes
- the reply format you use, with the marks

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-4
previous_reply_acts.text:
(two things to know)
- The five current jobs will still send their completion bells to me, and my parks on them will still wake this session. codex-17 has been told to poll those jobs instead. When my parks fire I'll reply in a line or two that codex-17 has it, to keep your Claude usage low. There's no way to cancel a park.
- I haven't parked on codex-17's job, so I won't spend usage watching it. Its status should come to you directly. If it doesn't arrive, you can check `GET /api/alpha/invoke/jobs/invoke-1790910049420-30079-b504795c`.
